newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Thursday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 2.58 billion yuan from 1.4 billion yuan on Tuesday with the 60-day contract the most actively traded.
The rates and turnover compared with those on Tuesday because the central bank did not issue figures for Wednesday.
Traders said trading was more active mainly due to the participation of the state banks, which had recently traded little due to a recent crackdown on the financial markets.

Lower interest rates on the interbank market against the state debt repurchase rates on the Shanghai stock exchange also made non-banking financial institutions including securities houses borrow more money on the interbank market, making volume go up, the traders said.
The Shanghai short-term financial centre, one of the money brokerages run by the central bank, was the most active trader on Thursday and was the biggest lender, traders said.
The Shandong short-term financing centre was the biggest borrower today, they said.
Traders said they believed the rates would continue to move narrowly around the current level in the short-term.
